How to tell good sushi from bad sushi before you order. Start with the rice, not the fish:
The rice should be just warm, about body temperature, and lightly seasoned with vinegar. Cold, packed rice means the kitchen treats sushi like an assembly line.
Look for a short menu that changes. Sixty kinds of fish all year usually means frozen fish. A dozen that change means they're buying what's good.

Check how much of the menu is nigiri (fish on rice) and how much is rolls. A menu of rolls with three sauces is selling something other than sushi.

And sit at the counter if there is one: you can ask what's good today.

If the chef puts the wasabi between the fish and the rice, you're somewhere serious.

What to order, from omakase to chirashi: https://www.savorscout.net/food/sushi
